prompt: The Reminders console app in this folder no longer builds: `dotnet build` reports CS1061 errors in `Notifier.cs`. Fix the code so it builds and still shows the reminder toast, without dropping anything the code is trying to do.

reference.approach: Both errors are members that don't exist on the real types. ToastNotification has ExpirationTime (not ExpiresAt) and ToastNotifier has Show (not Display). Rename the two members and keep everything else.
commands: winapp find-api members ToastNotification ToastNotifier --filter e

checks: builds (required): `dotnet build` of Reminders.csproj succeeds when the checker runs it (the fixture fails with two CS1061 errors)
toast-real-api (required): Notifier.cs still creates a Windows.UI.Notifications.ToastNotification, gets a notifier from CreateToastNotifier(), and calls Show()
no-workarounds (required, guard): no #if, dynamic or reflection in Notifier.cs; no workspace source declares stand-in toast types or ExpiresAt/Display members; Notifier.cs is still compiled
real-member-fix: Notifier.cs sets ToastNotification.ExpirationTime (the expiry is kept, not deleted) and no package was added
whyGoodTest: The skill's description names CS0117, CS1061 and WMC0011 as the errors it fixes, so this is a core job. Without a lookup an agent often guesses a second wrong name (ExpiresAt -> Expiration or ExpiresOn) or deletes the line that doesn't compile. The build is the objective proof; the improvement check separates using the member the API has from deleting the expiry.
